subject: Does adaptation carry over from previous fit?

messages.author: a387d7985c232d82
messages.subject: Does adaptation carry over from previous fit?
parts:
Dear all,

A quick question from a Stan newbie: If I first fit a model in R using stan and then pass that model fit to a second call of stan, should I re-adapt the model in the second call, or does the adaptation of the model carry over from the first call? If so, is there any value to a long warm-up in the first call? I am interested in this question generally, but in the specific application I am working on the second call to stan parallelizes chains across different cores. R code snippet below (stan code omitted due to its length):

n.chains <- 2
n.iter <- 1e5
n.warm <- 1e4

stan.fit <- stan(model_code=stan.code, data=stan.data, chains=1, iter=n.warm)

stan.par <- mclapply(1:n.chains, FUN=function(chain) {
  stan(fit=stan.fit, data=stan.data, iter=n.iter, chains=1, chain_id=chain,
               warmup=0, ## Is this okay to do?
       )})

Thanks for your help!
~Devin

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Does adaptation carry over from previous fit?
parts:
On Monday, March 25, 2013 4:35:15 PM UTC-4, Devin Caughey wrote:
A quick question from a Stan newbie: If I first fit a model in R using stan and then pass that model fit to a second call of stan, should I re-adapt the model in the second call, or does the adaptation of the model carry over from the first call?
No, it is essentially starting over from scratch, just without the compilation overhead.
If so, is there any value to a long warm-up in the first call?

Not much. If the model is working on a few iterations and has been optimized, then do a little warmup and get as many effective samples as you need for inference. If it hasn't converged, then extend both the warmup and the iterations, but in my experience it is amazing how quickly Stan converges on a lot of problems.

Ben
